name: ascet_find
description: Find saved names: components = owning Classes/Modules/State Machines; members = Methods/Processes and Variants; diagrams = BDE or State Machine Diagrams; objects = placed BDE nodes; states/transitions = topology. target is required. No source-body search.

inputSchema.description: For continuation, cursor is authoritative; other fields are ignored. Prefer only {cursor}.

cursor.description: Copy the short next_cursor handle unchanged. Send only cursor to this same tool. Never decode or edit it.

name.description: Name of the selected target. For an object or State, put its name here, never in scope.members. Omit to list.

components.description: Owning Class/Module/State Machine only: [{name:"ComponentName"}], [{path:"returned component_path"}] or [{ref:"returned ref"}]. Use name for a known short name; never guess full paths or Public/Private folders. Main is a Diagram, AEB_State_Off is a State, ES1130 is a Variant: none is a Component selector.

diagrams.description: Saved BDE or State Machine Diagram selectors. Resolve Main inside scope.components; returned Diagram refs preserve the exact owner and Diagram. State paths belong in find.name.

members.description: Exact saved Method/Process or full State/Transition path strings. Put this field inside scope, never at the root.

kinds.description: Exact saved source kinds inside scope. Text Method means method; BDE means diagram. Graphical Methods have diagram source kind, so discover their representation first.

variants.description: Exact saved Variant strings inside scope. ESDL source is ASDL. Preserve whitespace; omission includes all Variants, not a chosen implementation.

implementations.description: Exact saved Implementation OIDs, inside scope. Empty string is base; never invent base, null or a displayed name as an OID.

object_kinds.description: Native BDE object categories; only ascet_find target objects. Put object_kinds inside scope, not at the root.

scope.description: Every filter is inside scope: components, diagrams, members, kinds, variants, implementations, visibility, object_kinds. No filter fields at the request root.

cursor.description: Copy the short next_cursor handle unchanged. Send only cursor to this same tool. Never decode or edit it.

guidelines: Object/State names use name, never scope.members. Example: {target:"objects",name:"Stage",scope:{components:[{name:"Class"}],diagrams:[{name:"Main"}]}}. Add scope.object_kinds only for an explicitly requested declared BDE category, such as element or hierarchy; never guess hierarchy from a referenced Component, path or instance name. A Junction is State Machine topology: use target states and ascet_inspect_state, never object_kinds:["junction"]. An unknown variable is not an owning Component: find objects or search_bde first. Graphical member discovery must not force kind method; diagram_methods lists all members sharing that Diagram. Init may be Method, Process or Diagram.

Query saved ASCET source/BDE only. For an exclusively unsupported request (runtime values/scheduling, Dataset values, generated code, unsaved edits), immediately return outcome unsupported, intent.decision unsupported, evidence_refs:[] and facts containing only requested capability fields. Do not call find/search/read, including to confirm the symbol exists. For a mixed request, execute only the supported saved-code/BDE part and report the missing part explicitly.

Choose readers by returned read_tool/next_call, not by the owning Component name. All state_entry/state_static/state_exit and transition_trigger/transition_action/transition_condition text refs use ascet_read_code. State/Junction/Transition topology refs and *_binding refs use ascet_inspect_state. Diagram/placed-object refs use ascet_read_bde. Group a mixed ref list by read_tool and batch within each tool; never send Action code refs to inspect_state. Copy next_calls after an error; suggestions were not executed.

outcome located means all requested supported evidence was located and read; partial means required evidence is missing, ambiguous or paged content remains unread. Judge completion against the requested deliverables: a graphical Method needs its saved Diagram, not an invented or nonexistent text body. Do not downgrade a completed Diagram location/shared-Method task just because an additional external use is unverified; describe that caveat in answer. If the caller explicitly asks to verify that use, missing evidence makes the result partial. not_found requires a completed search in the requested scope. Saved assignments and connections do not prove runtime scheduling or a per-cycle execution rate.

Copy every user restriction into scope: owning Component, member, kind, Variant, Implementation, Diagram and visibility. Example: only Class.calc ASDL Method => {components:[{name:"Class"}],members:["calc"],kinds:["method"],variants:["ASDL"]}. A prior find does not scope later searches. Reuse the exact scope; change it only when the user changes the target. Selectors have one of name/path/ref; arrays are OR, fields are AND. When the caller asks for Variant candidates, put the exact saved strings in facts.variants (not a renamed helper field).

Find lists names, representations, language and Variant/Implementation candidates. If the caller explicitly says not to guess an owning Component/Method, ask for that owner before exploratory calls. Otherwise, if a referent is missing, or several candidates remain and the user asks to choose first, ask a direct question and leave the task unresolved (outcome partial when required). A clarification answer must contain a direct question mark (? or？). C candidates have language c; ASDL is ESDL. Preserve Variant strings exactly.

Copy actual ref strings, search_scope and next_call; never change a ref prefix/suffix. Only ref values identify citable objects; read_evidence.id is internal tracking, never a citation. Base Implementation is "". Keep facts associated with the same object ref and read_scope. Consume relevant pages; partial cannot prove absence.

BDE connections are saved facts, not runtime scheduling. Graphical Methods share their Diagram. Method bindings are structural facts, not source bodies. A cursor is pagination control, never evidence: keep cursor/next_cursor out of evidence_refs. evidence_refs contains only actual saved ref strings returned by a tool; for a local BDE page, use its citable_refs whitelist and never derive a ref suffix. The final response is exactly one JSON object with outcome, answer, evidence_refs, missing_evidence and facts; keep only caller-requested fields under facts. Do not add inference, inferred, saved, derived or other helper objects; put caveats in answer/missing_evidence. When has_more:true and complete coverage is requested, continuation_required/continuation_call identifies the required next step: call the same tool with exactly {cursor} until has_more:false; do not change queries, scope, direction or limit midway and then claim the original batch is complete. If replacing an incomplete search with a larger limit, copy the original queries and scope exactly, including omitted filters; do not add a guessed kind/member/Variant filter.

name: ascet_search_code
description: Search saved text code. Omit scope.kinds for an unspecified code/symbol search, including State/Transition Actions. Only an explicitly Method-only request requires scope.kinds:["method"]. Supports C/ESDL, Header, external C/H. queries are independent; identifier matches full symbols, text matches literals, regex matches patterns. Returns snippets and code refs with read_tool/next_call.

name: ascet_read_bde
description: Read whole Diagram listings or local BDE objects with real Pins/connections and Hierarchy boundaries. Object refs accept depth/direction; omit both for whole Diagram refs. For connections and initialization literals, read local object refs. Does not expand referenced Class implementations.

inputSchema.description: For continuation, cursor is authoritative; other fields are ignored. Prefer only {cursor}.

cursor.description: Copy the short next_cursor handle unchanged. Send only cursor to this same tool. Never decode or edit it.

depth.description: Object-local view: 0 = requested object interface only, 1/2 = one/two connection hops. Preserve an explicit user depth. At depth 0, connections and neighbors in that view are empty; do not broaden it to populate those fields.

direction.description: Which connections to include, relative to the requested object. outgoing does not change the requested object to the wire destination. Omit depth/direction for whole Diagram refs.

cursor.description: Copy the short next_cursor handle unchanged. Send only cursor to this same tool. Never decode or edit it.

guidelines: For a local object interface alone, use depth:0. For wiring, preserve the requested depth/direction. The requested object is the subject of the read: its ref, name, kind, hierarchy and complete Pin IDs belong under requested_object/facts.pin_ids; neighbors are only endpoint context and never replace it. Follow facts_mapping exactly: facts.pin_ids copies requested_object.pin_ids_on_page, never neighbors.endpoint_pins. If the caller says target/output/interface, keep the named object as the requested subject; report its own facts.pin_ids, and if the destination interface was also explicitly requested, report that separate object under target_interface/target_pin_ids rather than overwriting the requested-object facts. Omit object_kinds unless the caller supplied a native object category; hierarchy is a hierarchy category, not a generic synonym for element. A later read of another object does not change this association. depth:0 has connections:[] and neighbors:[]; keep that view. Derive names/counts from returned arrays; continue only relevant cursors, without a whole Diagram read for these facts.

name: ascet_inspect_state
description: Inspect saved State/Junction/Transition relationships, endpoints, priority, code_slots and Method bindings. Read returned Action code refs with ascet_read_code; locate the real bound Method to read its implementation.

inputSchema.description: For continuation, cursor is authoritative; other fields are ignored. Prefer only {cursor}.

cursor.description: Copy the short next_cursor handle unchanged. Send only cursor to this same tool. Never decode or edit it.
Copy the short next_cursor handle unchanged. Send only cursor to this same tool. Never decode or edit it.

guidelines: Transition inspection returns endpoint identities and saved Method bindings in code_slots. These bindings are references, not implementation bodies. For a request to verify a Transition, read the chosen Transition, both start_state and end_state refs, and every relevant binding ref; the inline method name is not proof that the binding ref was read. Read Action code refs with ascet_read_code; locate the real bound Method only when its implementation is requested. Batch independent reads. A deferred:true item has no facts yet: continue its own next_cursor on this tool.

Reuse the exact scope; change it only when the user changes the target. Selectors have one of name/path/ref; arrays are OR, fields are AND. When the caller asks for Variant candidates, put the exact saved strings in facts.variants (not a renamed helper field).

Find lists names, representations, language and Variant/Implementation candidates. If the caller explicitly says not to guess an owning Component/Method, ask for that owner before exploratory calls. Otherwise, if a referent is missing, or several candidates remain and the user asks to choose first, ask a direct question and leave the task unresolved (outcome partial when required). A clarification answer must contain a direct question mark (? or？). C candidates have language c; ASDL is ESDL. Preserve Variant strings exactly.

Copy actual ref strings, search_scope and next_call; never change a ref prefix/suffix. Only ref values identify citable objects; read_evidence.id is internal tracking, never a citation. Base Implementation is "". Keep facts associated with the same object ref and read_scope. Consume relevant pages; partial cannot prove absence.

BDE connections are saved facts, not runtime scheduling. Graphical Methods share their Diagram. Method bindings are structural facts, not source bodies. A cursor is pagination control, never evidence: keep cursor/next_cursor out of evidence_refs. evidence_refs contains only actual saved ref strings returned by a tool; for a local BDE page, use its citable_refs whitelist and never derive a ref suffix. The final response is exactly one JSON object with outcome, answer, evidence_refs, missing_evidence and facts; keep only caller-requested fields under facts. Do not add inference, inferred, saved, derived or other helper objects; put caveats in answer/missing_evidence. When has_more:true and complete coverage is requested, continuation_required/continuation_call identifies the required next step: call the same tool with exactly {cursor} until has_more:false; do not change queries, scope, direction or limit midway and then claim the original batch is complete. If replacing an incomplete search with a larger limit, copy the original queries and scope exactly, including omitted filters; do not add a guessed kind/member/Variant filter.
